entities.summary: Peter of Poitiers was a French scholastic theologian born in Poitiers around 1125–1130. He died in Paris on September 3, 1205. As a prominent figure in the Scholastic Movement, Peter of Poitiers contributed significantly to the development of Thomistic theology, particularly in the areas of metaphysics and the nature of God. His works, such as the Commentary on the Sentences of Peter Lombard, continue to influence Catholic theological thought to this day. Peter of Poitiers was also a key figure in the university town of Paris, where he taught and debated with other prominent scholars of his time. His interactions with other notable thinkers, including Thomas Aquinas, had a lasting impact on the intellectual landscape of medieval Europe. The Peter of Poitiers' legacy can be seen in the many universities and theological institutions that have followed in his footsteps, including the University of Paris, which remains one of the most prestigious institutions of higher learning in the world. Despite the passage of centuries, Peter of Poitiers' ideas continue to resonate with scholars and theologians, who seek to understand the intricacies of God's nature and the human condition. As a testament to his enduring influence, the Peter of Poitiers' writings have been translated into numerous languages and continue to be studied by scholars around the world.
